messages:
incidentbot: ALERT: Customer Orca Payments (dedicated pool: dp-eu1-42) p99 latency spike detected in eu-west-1. Current p95=420ms, p99=1.9s (SLO p99=750ms). Error rate stable <0.5%. Paging oncall. @oncall

Alice (oncall): Seeing the same on metrics. Tail latency trending up since 09:12 UTC. Rolling 5m avg p99 = 1.8s. Any recent deploys?

Ben (sre): No deploys reported for that pool. Telemetry shows heavy long-seq requests from a small set of tenant keys for Orca (tenants: orca-core, orca-reports). KV cache miss rate increased ~3x.

Carol (account-eng): Confirming Orca Payments says they have batch report jobs kicking off around 09:10 UTC. They just notified CS. Likely correlation.

Devin (cust-success): On call with Orca now, they're seeing slowness for payments reconciliation pages. Asking for ETA. They want mitigation ASAP and status updates.

Eve (infra): I can spin up warm spare nodes in eu-central and shift a fraction of traffic, but dedicated pool isolation rules mean we need to create a temporary fallback pool or route by region. Suggest: 1) throttle large batch endpoints for Orca by concurrency cap, 2) create dp-eu1-42-fallback in eu-central (same model), 3) route 30% traffic to fallback.

Frank (prod-ops): Agreed. Also recommend enabling request size cap (max tokens) for orca-reports and enabling prefix caching for reconciliation endpoints. That should reduce KV churn.

Alice (oncall): Action plan I will execute now: - apply concurrency cap to orca-reports via per-tenant policy (cap=6) - enable prefix caching for /v1/generate route for tenant orca-core - initiate fallback pool creation (Eve) - notify Orca with interim status (Devin)

Ben (sre): While you're doing that, I'm going to run a quick flamegraph on serving runtime and collect KV cache hit/miss for dp-eu1-42. Snippet: ```curl -s "https://metrics.internal/pools/dp-eu1-42/kvcache?window=5m"```

Eve (infra): Spawning dp-eu1-42-fallback: creation started, estimated ready 4 mins. I will open routing ticket to send 30% traffic (weighted LB split).

Carol (account-eng): Noting customer contract: SLO credits may apply if p99 > 750ms for >10 minutes. Let's aim to bring p99 < 900ms asap to avoid escalation. I'm ready to brief their security/ops if they request a postmortem.

Devin (cust-success): Told Orca we're throttling batch job concurrency and shifting some traffic to fallback in eu-central. They acknowledged and asked to be pinged when p99 < 1s. They also provided a sample job payload if you need it.

Alice (oncall): Concurrency cap applied to orca-reports. Observability: p95 now 390ms, p99 dropped to 1.4s (improvement). Continuing with cache change.

Ben (sre): KV cache miss-rate pre-change: 28%. After prefix caching enabled: 13% and reducing. Flamegraph shows hot loop inside attention kernel on long sequences — a few requests >8k tokens.

Frank (prod-ops): Can we enforce max tokens for reconciliation endpoint to 2048 for now? That will protect tail.

Alice (oncall): Enforcing max_tokens=2048 for tenant orca-reports. Immediate effect: p99 -> 980ms, p95=360ms. Still above SLO but trending.

Eve (infra): dp-eu1-42-fallback is ready, routing change applied (30% to fallback). Fallback pool p99 currently 620ms. Total combined p99 computed ~780ms.

Ben (sre): Running additional mitigation: temporarily lower batch size on worker side for orca-core long jobs. Also kick off a lightweight model variant for huge inputs (quantized variant) as a fallback.

Carol (account-eng): Orca appreciates the quick action. They've paused non-critical reconciliation jobs on their side after our ask. They will keep us updated if anything else spikes.

Devin (cust-success): Customer-facing message sent: "Investigating high latency for reconciliation/reporting. We've applied throttles and traffic steering; you may see improved performance in ~10 mins. We'll follow up with full context and mitigation details."

Alice (oncall): Monitoring 10m window. p95=340ms, p99=720ms (just below SLO). Keeping thread open until stable 30m. Logging mitigation steps for postmortem.

Frank (prod-ops): Filing incident ticket and tagging for postmortem with runbook: include sequence-length quotas, per-tenant concurrency caps, fallback pool automation, and customer notification timeline.

incidentbot: RESOLVED: p99 for Orca Payments dp-eu1-42 returned below SLO at 10:02 UTC after combined mitigations (concurrency cap, token cap, prefix caching, fallback routing). Incident duration ~50m.

Devin (cust-success): Sent closure note to Orca and arranged a follow-up meeting tomorrow for runbook review and to discuss workload pattern smoothing.

Alice (oncall): Closing thread. Will upload graphs and timeline to the incident tracker. Thanks all. :tada:"
